over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Exela Technologies, Inc. (renamed successor of Quinpario Acquisition Corp. 2) realized record, ~3-5-year horizon (~2020-2022)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier contains no information about
> how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status and filer identity (feasibility-relevant)
- The SEC registrant that closed the 2017 business combination retained the same CIK
  (0001620179) and continued as a reporting company under its new name; EDGAR records
  the former name "Quinpario Acquisition Corp. 2" effective through 2017-07-12 and the
  current name "Exela Technologies, Inc." thereafter — there was no deregistration or
  CIK change. [SRC: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001620179.json]
- The realized-record source used here is Exela Technologies, Inc.'s Form 10-K for
  fiscal year 2021, filed 2022-03-16 (approximately 4.6 years after the July 12, 2017
  closing, within the fixed ~2020-2022 outcome window). [SRC: SEC accession
  0001558370-22-003779, Form 10-K FY2021]

## Segment / business-line disclosure in the outcome window
- For fiscal year 2021 the Company reported "three reportable segments": Information &
  Transaction Processing Solutions ("ITPS"), Healthcare Solutions ("HS"), and Legal &
  Loss Prevention Services ("LLPS") — the same three segment names used for SourceHOV's
  pre-combination business lines. ITPS was "our largest segment, with $874.1 million of
  revenues for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2021, representing 74.9% of our
  revenues." [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-22-003779, Form 10-K FY2021]
- The FY2021 10-K uses "we," "us," or "our" to refer to "Exela Technologies, Inc. and
  its consolidated subsidiaries, and where applicable, our predecessors SourceHOV and
  Novitex prior to the closing of the Novitex Business Combination," but does not
  present Novitex's pre-combination Digital Services / Document Logistics lines as a
  separate reportable segment or subsidiary note distinct from the three
  SourceHOV-derived segments. [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-22-003779, Form 10-K
  FY2021]
- No discontinued-operations disclosure or divestiture of the SourceHOV or Novitex
  predecessor businesses was found in this filing; the only reference to divestiture is
  a generic debt-covenant risk-factor statement that indebtedness "may... require
  non-strategic divestitures," not a description of an occurred event. [SRC: SEC
  accession 0001558370-22-003779, Form 10-K FY2021]

## Realized financial trajectory within the window
- Consolidated revenue for the year ended December 31, 2021 was $1,166.6 million,
  described as a decrease of "$126.0 million, or 9.7%," from $1,292.6 million for the
  year ended December 31, 2020. [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-22-003779, Form 10-K
  FY2021]
- Net loss was $142.4 million for fiscal year 2021, compared to a net loss of $178.5
  million for fiscal year 2020. [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-22-003779, Form 10-K
  FY2021]
- Goodwill of $358.3 million represented 34.6% of total consolidated assets as of
  December 31, 2021; the Company's annual goodwill-impairment tests as of October 1,
  2021 and October 1, 2020 both concluded "there was no impairment." [SRC: SEC accession
  0001558370-22-003779, Form 10-K FY2021]
- The filing discloses that "substantial doubt regarding the Company's ability to meet
  its obligation as they become due within one year... which was raised by management
  prior to the second quarter of 2021, is not applicable" as of the filing date, after
  the Company "raised $406.8 million in gross proceeds from equity financings" and
  "reduced indebtedness by $338.5 million" during 2021. [SRC: SEC accession
  0001558370-22-003779, Form 10-K FY2021]

## Corporate/capital-structure events within the window
- Stockholders authorized a reverse stock split at the Company's 2020 Annual Meeting;
  the Board of Directors set the ratio at one-for-three effective January 25, 2021, and
  Common Stock began trading on Nasdaq on a split-adjusted basis January 26, 2021, with
  no change to the ticker symbol. [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-22-003779, Form 10-K
  FY2021]
- The FY2021 10-K's risk factors state that "during 2022, we failed to meet the
  requirement that our minimum bid price exceed $1.00 for at least 30 consecutive
  business days" under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) and "received a letter from
  Nasdaq regarding the infraction," with no assurance the Company would remedy the
  deficiency and remain listed. [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-22-003779, Form 10-K
  FY2021]

## Items sought but not found
- No source was located that separately isolates a post-close financial or operating
  trajectory specifically for the Novitex-derived product/asset lines (as distinct from
  the SourceHOV-derived ITPS/HS/LLPS segment structure) within the ~2020-2022 window;
  whether this reflects operational absorption of Novitex's offerings into the
  SourceHOV-named segments, a reporting/naming choice, or something else is not
  addressed by the filing and is recorded as [UNVERIFIED]. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The renamed successor entity (Exela Technologies, Inc., same CIK) remained a public
  reporting company through the fixed ~2020-2022 outcome window, disclosing consolidated
  segment and financial results but no filing-level separation of the two 2017 predecessor
  businesses' individual post-close trajectories. [SRC: SEC accession
  0001558370-22-003779, Form 10-K FY2021]
- The best-documented realized scalar is a continued consolidated net loss narrowing from
  $178.5 million (FY2020) to $142.4 million (FY2021) on declining revenue ($1,292.6
  million to $1,166.6 million), alongside a temporarily disclosed going-concern doubt
  (raised before Q2 2021, stated resolved after a $406.8 million equity raise and $338.5
  million debt reduction during 2021) and a 2022 Nasdaq minimum-bid-price compliance
  notice. [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-22-003779, Form 10-K FY2021]

[SLICE END]
